name: Pickled, fermented and brined vegetables
anchor: Per-produce-class sovereign maximum levels for lead and cadmium (EU Reg. 2023/915 and Switzerland VHK 817.022.15; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2; AU-NZ Schedule 19; MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel MOH FCS-2016), nickel under EU Reg. 2024/1987, total and inorganic arsenic under MERCOSUR and Israel MOH FCS-2016, and total mercury under Hong Kong Cap. 132V and Israel MOH FCS-2016.
native_basis_label: drained product as sold, wet weight, brine and packing liquid excluded from the analytical portion
scope_note: Vegetables preserved by acidification, lactic fermentation or brining and sold as such: cucumber pickles and gherkins, sauerkraut, kimchi, pickled onions, beetroot and radish, giardiniera and mixed pickles, olives cured for table use, and pickled peppers. THE BASIS IS THE DRAINED PRODUCT: brine and packing liquid are excluded from the analytical portion, which matches the AU-NZ 'portion ordinarily consumed' construction and the Hong Kong Cap. 132V pickled-cucumber row, and which prevents a lightly-loaded brine from diluting a result. Water content of the drained product is comparable to the fresh vegetable for cucumbers, cabbage and onions, so fresh-basis vegetable maximum levels are comparable at face value; table olives are naturally lower in moisture and carry their own sovereign rows, which are named. OUT OF SCOPE: fermented soy products, soy sauce, fish sauce and vinegar (Category 32); preserved tomato products, including canned and heat-sterilised tomatoes, passata and pickled green tomatoes (Category 32 tomato-condiments), which is why the Hong Kong heat-treated hermetically sealed tomato row at 50 ug/kg is not an anchor here; pickled fruit and chutneys whose predominant ingredient is fruit (fruit-snacks row, or Category 7 for condiment forms); pickled fish and seafood (Category 6); fermented dairy (Category 24); products marketed for ages 0 to 5 (Category 1). Where the certified presentation is a hermetically sealed tinplate can, the canned-foods tin maximum level applies as a hard stop through the tin control below. COLLAPSED SOVEREIGN SPLIT: Hong Kong sets lead at 100 ug/kg for pickled cucumbers and 400 ug/kg for table olives, MERCOSUR and Paraguay set 500 ug/kg for table olives, and Switzerland sets cadmium at 20 ug/kg for table olives with no pickled-vegetable row at all. The row binds the strictest applicable value in each cell, which means the fermented brassica products (sauerkraut, kimchi) are held to a cadmium value written for table olives and the table olives are held to a lead value written for pickled cucumbers. Splitting table olives out of this row is the recommended taxonomy fix.
basis_guard: wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|as listed|product as offered to consumer|product as placed on market|as sold|as_sold|as consumed|commodity|edible part
basis_guard_note: Every named anchor for this row must sit in a dietary as-sold, wet-weight, edible-part or portion-ordinarily-consumed basis. The guard rejects the register's article and material bases (toy and food-contact migration, textile and leather extraction, fertiliser and growing-media dry matter, colour-additive ingredient specifications, animal-feed 12 percent moisture), any one of which would be a basis conflation if it anchored a food row. The drained-product construction is what makes the fresh-vegetable bases comparable here; brine is excluded from the analytical portion rather than averaged into it.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only; the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for the row's product form in the row's native basis, a disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination, or a control; never occurrence-derived)

stricter_unselected.scope: Tomatoes, preserved by heat treatment and hermet

Pb.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 9 sets lead at 100 ug/kg for pickled cucumbers specifically and for canned vegetables, and Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 20 sets 100 ug/kg for preserved vegetables; the table-olive carve-outs sit at 400 ug/kg (Hong Kong) and 500 ug/kg (MERCOSUR and Paraguay) and the Israeli preserved brassica and leafy row at 300 ug/kg.
Pb.substantiation: Hong Kong writes a pickled-cucumber lead row, so the exact cell is directly regulated for the dominant product form in this row and the cell is a government maximum level rather than a read-across. The row binds the strictest applicable value, 100 ug/kg, and the consequence is disclosed: table olives are held to a value four to five times stricter than the 400 to 500 ug/kg their own sovereign rows allow, reflecting the lye-curing and brine-contact history that those rows accommodate. HONG KONG'S OWN TREATMENT OF THE PICKLED FORM IS THE POINT OF THIS CELL: a pickled cucumber is a cucurbit fruiting vegetable, for which Hong Kong sets 50 ug/kg fresh, yet Hong Kong deliberately writes pickled cucumbers at 100 ug/kg, which is the regulator's own recognition that acidification and brine contact add a pathway the fresh value does not cover. The fresh fruiting-vegetable value is therefore not the applicable cell for this row. AUDIT DISPOSITIONS. This row's audit scan was widened to see the fresh vegetable commodity classes (the same widening that corrected the total-arsenic cell), and it now reports five credible rows at 50 ug/kg, all of them fresh or heat-sterilised forms. Each is dispositioned rather than left silent. (1) hk_cap132v_pb_fruiting-vegetables-cucurbits_50 and (2) hk_cap132v_pb_fruiting-vegetables-other-than-cucurbits_50 are Hong Kong's own FRESH fruiting-vegetable classes. The same instrument separately and expressly writes pickled cucumbers at 100 ug/kg and canned vegetables at 100 ug/kg, so Hong Kong has itself ruled that the preserved form is not governed by its fresh classes; both of the express preserved-form rows are named in this cell. (3) il_fcs2016_pb_3_4_fruiting_vegetables_including_tomato_cucumber_pepper_50 is Israel's fresh fruiting-vegetable category. Israel likewise writes an express preserved-form carve-out, category 20 'Canned vegetables, except listed categories' at 100 ug/kg and category 20.1 'Canned brassica and leafy vegetables' at 300 ug/kg, and this cell names category 20; the canned and jarred presentations that make up this row therefore sit in category 20 under Israeli law, not in the fresh category 3.4. (4) hk_cap132v_pb_tomatoes-preserved-by-heat-treatment-and-hermetically-s_50 governs heat-sterilised canned tomato product, not acidified, fermented or brined vegetables; preserved tomato products including canned tomatoes, passata and pickled green tomatoes route to Category 32 tomato-condiments and are expressly out of this row's scope. (5) ch_vhk_2026_pb_fruchtgemuse_50 is the only one of the five that is not disposed of by its own instrument's text, and it is recorded as an open interpretive call rather than passed over. The Swiss VHK 817.022.15 annex writes per-commodity FRESH vegetable classes and, for LEAD, no pickled, brined, fermented or canned vegetable class at all; the annex does write preserved-form rows for other analytes where it intends them (Tafeloliven cadmium 20 ug/kg, which is this row's binding cadmium anchor; Lebensmittelkonserven tin; getrocknete Bohnen nickel), so its silence on preserved vegetables for lead is a gap in coverage rather than an express extension of the fresh class. The value is not adopted because, unlike total arsenic, lead is an analyte on which sovereign regulators HAVE ruled on the pickled and canned form, and they have ruled uniformly: Hong Kong pickled cucumbers 100 ug/kg, Hong Kong canned vegetables 100 ug/kg, Israel canned vegetables 100 ug/kg. Reading the Swiss fresh Fruchtgemuese class onto a brined product would extend an instrument to a form it does not address, against the uniform contrary treatment of the two instruments that do address it, and would publish 50 ug/kg for a product form for which no sovereign anywhere has written a value below 100 ug/kg. THE CONTRAST WITH THIS ROW'S TOTAL-ARSENIC CELL IS DELIBERATE AND IS THE TEST THIS CATEGORY APPLIES: no sovereign writes any pickled-form arsenic value, so for arsenic the fresh commodity class is the only reading available and it is also the conservative one, which is why that cell now binds 100 ug/kg from the MERCOSUR cucurbit and bulb classes. Where sovereigns have ruled on the processed form, the ruling governs; where none has, the commodity class governs. The canned-vegetable rows of Hong Kong and Israel ARE named here, because canned and jarred presentations of sauerkraut and table olives are squarely in this row.

Cd.basis: drained product as sold, wet weight
Cd.label: Switzerland VHK 817.022.15 sets cadmium at 20 ug/kg for table olives, the only sovereign cadmium maximum level written for a product form in this row; Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 6 covers the remaining pickled and fermented vegetables through its residual vegetables row at 100 ug/kg.
Cd.substantiation: The Swiss table-olive cadmium row is not an isolated outlier: the same annex sets 20 ug/kg for fruiting vegetables, legume vegetables and pome, stone and citrus fruit, so table olives sit at the schedule's normal level for a fruit-type edible rather than at a specially strict one. Table olives are named in this taxonomy row, so 20 ug/kg is applicable to it and is the strictest applicable value. The five-fold consequence for sauerkraut, kimchi and pickled onions is disclosed, and splitting table olives into their own row is the recommended taxonomy fix.

tAs.basis: drained product as sold, wet weight
tAs.label: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 set total arsenic at 100 ug/kg for the Cucurbitaceae and other fruiting-vegetable classes and for bulb vegetables and sheathing leaves, which are the commodity classes of the pickled cucumbers, gherkins, pickled peppers and pickled onions that dominate this row; the same instrument sets 200 ug/kg for roots and tubers, 300 ug/kg for brassica and leaf vegetables and 300 ug/kg for table olives, and Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 2 sets 500 ug/kg for vegetables. The row binds the strictest applicable value, 100 ug/kg.
tAs.substantiation: R1 direct maximum levels; the row binds the strictest applicable to any member. WHY THE COMMODITY CLASSES REACH THE PICKLED FORM UNDER THIS INSTRUMENT. MERCOSUR writes separate rows where it intends a processed form to have its own value: table olives and tomato concentrates each get one. It writes NO pickled-cucumber, sauerkraut, kimchi or pickled-onion row, and its vegetable classes are written without a 'fresh' qualifier ('fruiting vegetables of the Cucurbitaceae family', 'bulb vegetables and sheathing leaves'), in contrast to its fruit classes, which are expressly 'fresh fruits excluding berries and small fruits'. A pickled cucumber is a fruiting vegetable of the Cucurbitaceae family, so under MERCOSUR it sits in that class at 100 ug/kg, and a pickled onion sits in the bulb class at 100 ug/kg. This is the same canon of construction this category applies to Israel for dried fruit: where an instrument demonstrably knows how to write a carve-out for a processed form and declines to, the commodity class governs. CORRECTION OF RECORD: an earlier draft of this cell published 300 ug/kg on the table-olive rows alone, with Hong Kong vegetables at 500 ug/kg as the only other named candidate. Table olives are one member of this row; the dominant members had no named candidate at all, and the fresh commodity classes three times stricter were named nowhere and dispositioned nowhere. The row's scan could not surface them because its audit_scope carried only pickle, ferment and olive tokens and its exclusion list carried a bare 'fruit' token that also matched 'fruiting vegetables'; both have been widened and narrowed respectively so the scan can now see these rows. CONSISTENCY WITH THIS ROW'S OTHER ARSENIC CELL: the inorganic-arsenic cell already applies exactly this reasoning, reading 60 ug/kg across from the fresh fruits-and-vegetables class on the ground that acidification, fermentation and brining do not create or concentrate arsenic in the drained product. That argument is analyte-level, not species-level, so it applies with identical force to total arsenic; publishing 300 ug/kg for total arsenic while reading 60 ug/kg across for the species was internally contradictory. THE LEAD CELL IS DIFFERENT ON PURPOSE AND THAT IS NOT A CONTRADICTION: there, Hong Kong writes an express pickled-cucumber lead row at 100 ug/kg against its fresh cucurbit value of 50 ug/kg, so a sovereign has expressly ruled that brine contact adds a lead pathway the fresh value does not cover, and the express pickled row is the applicable cell. No sovereign writes any pickled-form arsenic row, so no such ruling exists for arsenic and the commodity class governs. CONSEQUENCE, DISCLOSED: the table-olive members are held at 100 ug/kg against the 300 ug/kg their own MERCOSUR class allows, which is the same strictest-member over-compliance this row already applies to lead (table olives held at the pickled-cucumber value) and cadmium (fermented brassicas held at the table-olive value). Splitting table olives out of this row is the recommended taxonomy fix. Total arsenic is never satisfied by the inorganic-arsenic cell; both are reported, and the 60 ug/kg species value remains the operative arsenic constraint.

iAs.basis: drained product as sold, wet weight

sovereign_floor.basis: drained product as sold, wet weight

floor_cell.rationale: No in-force sovereign or general-food iAs maximum level applies to this product on the dietary-content basis after the supersession of regulations/israel-moh-fcs-2016-heavy-metals-tin-food-guidelines; the species is bounded by its parent total (tAs) per the certification-readiness ruling (species ≤ total).

iAs.rationale: Published iAs of 60 ug/kg is retained as a precautionary program value after the instrument that carried it (il_fcs2016_ias_3_fruits_and_vegetables_including_mushrooms_edible_pla_60) was superseded; the strictest in-force sovereign floor is the parent total that bounds iAs. HMTc is a ratcheting program and does not loosen a live limit because an instrument died.
iAs.label: Precautionary: 60 ug/kg, below the sovereign floor of 100 ug/kg (mercosur_gmc12_2011_cucurbitaceae_fruiting_vegetables_tas_100). The floor is the strictest in-force government maximum level; the program number is a disclosed policy choice, not a claim about the law.

tHg.basis: Hong Kong vegetable total-mercury maximum level applied to the drained pickled product as sold (comparable basis, disclosed)
tHg.label: No jurisdiction writes a total-mercury maximum level for pickled, fermented or brined vegetables; the nearest applicable sovereign value is Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 12 for vegetables other than edible fungi, 10 ug/kg, the strictest sovereign total-mercury maximum level for the underlying commodity.
tHg.substantiation: R2 disclosed read-across from the same commodity in its fresh form, taken at face value on the comparable drained-product basis. Selecting the stricter of the two available vegetable total-mercury values (Hong Kong 10 ug/kg rather than Israel 30 ug/kg) keeps the read-across in the conservative direction.

MeHg.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury maximum level for this product form, and no not-material determination is supportable for it: the routed corpus quantifies methylmercury in edible plant and fungal tissue (wang2021-houttuynia-mercury-china measured methylmercury in the leaf and root tissue of an edible leafy vegetable at an LOD of 0.002 ug/kg; stasinos2014-heavy-metals-tubers-review in root and tuber tissue; asensio2023-madrid-mushrooms-mercury), so the species is not absent from produce and the biological premise of a not-material determination is rebutted inside this very category. Every fresh vegetable class this row derives from (leafy, non-root and root/tuber) carries quantified methylmercury in the routed corpus and is held under the same control, and no evidence supports asserting that anaerobic brine fermentation is a methylation-free compartment; control is the fail-safe treatment where the affirmative claim is unsupported. Methylmercury is therefore held under mandatory analytical control rather than recorded not-material, and it remains bounded by identity below the published total-mercury ceiling for this row (read-across from Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 12, 10 ug/kg); methylmercury cannot exceed total mercury. No methylmercury ceiling is invented.
MeHg.reference_method: Methylmercury by GC-ICP-MS or EN 16801, required only on a lot whose total mercury reaches 60 percent of the published total-mercury ceiling; any quantifiable methylmercury on such a lot is investigated and the lot is held pending root-cause analysis.

Ni.basis: EU fruiting-vegetable nickel maximum level applied to the drained pickled product as sold (comparable basis, disclosed)
Ni.label: EU Reg. 2024/1987 writes no maximum level for pickled, fermented or brined vegetables; the nearest applicable sovereign value is its fruiting-vegetable row, 400 ug/kg, which governs the cucumbers and peppers that are the dominant raw material of this row and is the strictest nickel value the instrument sets for any vegetable class it contains.
Ni.substantiation: R2 disclosed read-across from the same commodity in its fresh form. The instrument's own bulb (900), brassica (500) and legume (1000) rows are looser and would each be applicable to some member of this row, so selecting the 400 ug/kg fruiting-vegetable value keeps the read-across in the conservative direction and holds the whole row to the strictest class value rather than the loosest.

Sn.rationale: Tin in this row is a packaging-migration analyte rather than a property of the food. Every sovereign tin maximum level in the register is conditioned on a canned (tinplate) presentation, and this row contains presentations at both extremes: table olives and sauerkraut are still widely packed in hermetically sealed tinplate, while pickles, kimchi and giardiniera are predominantly glass-jarred. Because the row's presentation determines whether any sovereign tin limit applies at all, HMTc publishes no standalone tin number for the row and instead makes the screen mandatory with an escalation to the canned-foods maximum level whenever the certified presentation is tinplate.
Sn.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every lot. Where the certified presentation is a tinplate can or a metal-lined closure, the canned-foods maximum level (EU Reg. 2023/915, 200000 ug/kg) applies as a regulatory hard stop and the lot is additionally tested at end of shelf life; where the presentation is glass, pouch or plastic, any result above 50 ug/kg is investigated for a metal-contact source.

companions.scope: canned foods other than canned beverages, except canned dried and canned

Al.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for any fruit, vegetable or produce form in any jurisdiction. The register's aluminium limits are drinking-water and bottled-water parameters, infant-formula maximum levels, a food-contact plastics specific migration limit, toy migration limits, and permitted-additive levels for baked and starch foods; none of them regulates aluminium as a contaminant of produce. Aluminium is also the third most abundant element in the earth's crust and appears in produce largely as soil-derived and root-associated mineral content rather than as process contamination, so no near-neighbour read-across is supportable either. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone aluminium number for this row.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every lot, reported to the applicant. Document any aluminium-containing processing aid, packaging contact or anti-caking agent, comply with the additive rules of every market of sale, and investigate any result that is an outlier against the applicant's own lot history.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium is recorded as a SCREEN, not a protective ceiling. Dietary chromium is dominated by nutritionally essential Cr(III); the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), controlled separately by reflex speciation. The screen is excluded from the firm-limit count.
Cr.basis: Hong Kong vegetable total-chromium maximum level applied to the drained pickled product as sold (comparable basis, disclosed)
Cr.label: No jurisdiction writes a total-chromium maximum level for pickled, fermented or brined vegetables; the nearest applicable sovereign value is Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7 for vegetables other than pulses, 500 ug/kg, the only dietary total-chromium maximum level in the register that reaches this commodity.
Cr.substantiation: R2 disclosed read-across from the same commodity in its fresh form, on the comparable drained-product basis, recorded as a screen rather than a protective ceiling. Acidified and fermented matrices are the strongest case in this category for chromium(VI) reduction to chromium(III), which is why the species cell is a substantiated not-material determination controlled by reflex speciation.

Cr-VI.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum level for any solid food in any jurisdiction. The register's only INGESTED Cr(VI) parameters are drinking-water maxima (Australia NHMRC 2025, 50 ug/L, nhmrc2025_crvi_drinking_water_50; California SWRCB, 10 ug/L, us_ca_swrcb_2024_cr-vi_chromium-hexavalent_mcl_10ugl and ca_swrcb_crvi_drinking_water_10), which are water-basis parameters expressed per litre of a consumed liquid and supply no applicable ceiling for a solid produce row in this row's native basis; every remaining Cr(VI) row in the register is an article or material limit (toys, textiles, leather, fertilisers, electrical equipment). Chromium in produce is dominated by nutritionally essential Cr(III), and Cr(VI) is not stable in the plant matrix: fruit and vegetable tissue is an aqueous, organic-acid and ascorbate-rich reducing medium in which Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III), so a reported Cr(VI) value in this matrix reflects extraction conditions rather than the chromium species the consumer ingests. Hexavalent chromium is therefore bounded by the published total-chromium screen for this row (read-across from Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7, 500 ug/kg) and controlled by reflex speciation rather than by a published number.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every lot. Any total-chromium result at or above 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation by EN 15192 or EPA 6800 IC-ICP-MS isotope dilution; any quantifiable Cr(VI) at LOQ fails the lot. Cr(VI) is never published as a panel number.
Cr-VI.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a Cr(VI) maximum level for any solid food. The register's ingested Cr(VI) parameters are drinking-water maxima only (AU NHMRC 50 ug/L; California SWRCB 10 ug/L), which are water-basis and do not reach produce; every other Cr(VI) row is an article or material limit (EU 2009/48 toys, EU 2018/1513 textiles, EU 301/2014 leather, EU 2019/1009 fertilisers, EU RoHS). Neither drinking-water issuer is admitted to this category's credible set as a food regulator for a solid produce row. The total-chromium parent for this row is published.
